# DRAFT: Medical device adverse incident report

> This is a draft for human review. It has not been submitted. A manufacturer would report
> through the MHRA MORE portal; healthcare professionals and users report through the Yellow Card scheme.

## 1. Device
- Name: ClinicDrift-monitored DR screening model
- Version: v1.0
- Intended use: screening retinal photographs for referable diabetic retinopathy

## 2. Where and when
- Clinic: US-WEAR-01 (United States)
- Period: week 8 (starting 2026-02-23)

## 3. What happened
ClinicDrift detected significant data drift, indicating that retinal images from this clinic no longer match the characteristics of the data on which the artificial intelligence (AI) model was validated. The observed drift score reached 0.99, where 0.5 indicates data consistent with the training baseline and 1 indicates a clear divergence.

Because of this drift, the model's catch rate (sensitivity for referable diabetic retinopathy) cannot be verified from the 50 scans obtained during this week. Independent expert grades for this batch are not yet available. The AI model referred 52% of scans this week, compared to a baseline referral rate of 41% in the training data.

## 4. Potential patient impact
As the catch rate cannot be verified, the number of potentially missed cases cannot be estimated. No patient harm has been confirmed at this time.

## 5. Likely cause
A severe reduction in image sharpness and overall image quality has been identified. This is likely attributable to camera defocus, optical contamination (such as a dirty lens), or operator error during image capture. (Category: camera or image quality; confidence 90%; source: gemini).

Evidence:
- The drift score reached 0.99 (where 0.5 reflects training data characteristics and 1.0 indicates clear divergence).
- Mean sharpness decreased by 90.9%, falling from 31.8 in the training set to 2.91 during the flagged period.
- Mean image quality decreased by 47.5%, falling from 0.875 in the training set to 0.459 during the flagged period.
- The referral rate increased from 0.414 in the training set to 0.52 at the clinic (+25.5% relative change) across 50 scans, whilst image resolution remained constant at 1020.0 pixels.

## 6. Action
ClinicDrift suspended AI deployment at this clinic because the input images have drifted beyond the validated operating range, meaning device sensitivity cannot currently be verified. It is recommended that all scans from this clinic be routed to human graders for manual evaluation until the following investigations are completed:

Checks:
- [ ] Inspect and clean the camera objective lens to remove dust, smudges, or oil.
- [ ] Check and verify the calibration of the camera's autofocus or manual focus mechanisms.
- [ ] Review operator acquisition protocols, including focusing techniques and patient positioning.
- [ ] Audit recent flagged scans to confirm the presence of blur or defocus artefacts.

## 7. Regulatory context
- Post-market surveillance (PMS): this alert was generated as part of ongoing proactive monitoring of the device in clinical use.
- Predetermined change control plan (PCCP): any software or model modifications undertaken in response must align with an agreed PCCP.
- MHRA AI Airlock Phase 2 report: refer to recommendations 3 and 4.

## 8. MIT AI Risk Repository tags
- 7.3 AI system safety, failures & limitations > Lack of capability or robustness
- 1.3 Discrimination & toxicity > Unequal performance across groups
- 5.1 Human-computer interaction > Overreliance and unsafe use
